concepts.title: Azure Resource Hierarchy & RBAC Least Privilege
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Manage Azure identities and governance
concepts.plainEnglish: Azure organizes resources in a strict hierarchy: Management Group -> Subscription -> Resource Group -> Resource. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permissions inherit downward, so assigning a role at a higher scope grants it to everything below.
concepts.whyItMatters: AVD relies on scoped RBAC—for example, Desktop Virtualization User on an Application Group for end users, and Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor on the subscription or resource group for Start VM on Connect.
gotchas: RBAC is additive; there is no explicit Deny in standard RBAC (Deny comes from Azure Blueprints/Deployment Stacks or Deny Assignments).
Assigning Owner/Contributor at subscription level violates least privilege and breaks separation of duties across control planes.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which built-in RBAC role is required by the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal to power on deallocated session hosts for Start VM on Connect?
choices: Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor
checkQuestion.explanation: Start VM on Connect requires assigning the Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor role to the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal at the subscription or resource group scope.

concepts.title: VNets, Subnets, NSGs & Private DNS Zones
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Configure and manage virtual networking
concepts.plainEnglish: A Virtual Network (VNet) is your isolated IP space in Azure, carved into subnets. Network Security Groups (NSGs) filter traffic at subnet or NIC level, while Private Link + Private DNS Zones keep traffic to PaaS services (like Azure Files or AVD) on private IPs instead of the public internet.
concepts.whyItMatters: In an AVD landing zone, session hosts sit in a dedicated spoke subnet (`10.100.x.x`), Private Endpoints sit in a separate subnet, and Private DNS Zones resolve `privatelink.file.core.windows.net` and `privatelink.wvd.microsoft.com` internally.
gotchas: Forgetting to link the Private DNS Zone to the spoke (or hub) VNet causes session hosts to resolve the public IP instead of the Private Endpoint.
NSGs are stateful, but asymmetric routing through a hub Azure Firewall without UDRs or proper DNS breaks Private Link.

checkQuestion.prompt: You deployed a Private Endpoint for your FSLogix Azure Files storage account, but session hosts still resolve the storage account FQDN to a public IP. What is most likely missing?
choices: A Public IP on each session host
A Virtual Network Link connecting the privatelink.file.core.windows.net Private DNS Zone to the VNet
checkQuestion.explanation: Private Endpoints require a Private DNS Zone (e.g., privatelink.file.core.windows.net) linked to the VNet where DNS queries originate.

concepts.title: Azure Storage Accounts & Azure Files Performance Tiers
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Implement and manage storage
concepts.plainEnglish: Azure Files provides managed SMB file shares in the cloud. Standard tiers (Transaction Optimized / Hot / Cool on GPv2) are HDD-backed with shared IOPS limits, whereas Premium (`FileStorage` / `Premium_LRS` or `Premium_ZRS`) is SSD-backed and scales IOPS and throughput directly with the provisioned share size in GiB/TiB.
concepts.whyItMatters: FSLogix profiles are VHDX files mounted over SMB. During morning logon storms, IOPS and sub-10ms latency determine whether 100 users sign in smoothly or freeze on a black screen.
gotchas: On Premium Azure Files, a tiny 100 GiB share has very low baseline IOPS—provisioned capacity drives performance.
Standard_LRS is often fine for a 2-person lab, but fails under multi-user logon storms.

checkQuestion.prompt: On Premium Azure Files (FileStorage), what directly increases your share's baseline IOPS and throughput?
choices: Adding more CPU cores to the session hosts
Switching from Entra ID join to AD DS join
checkQuestion.explanation: Premium Azure Files uses a provisioned capacity model: baseline IOPS, burst IOPS, and throughput scale linearly with the provisioned share size.

concepts.title: Host Pools, Session Hosts, App Groups & Workspaces
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: AVD separates compute from user publishing using four linked objects: Session Hosts (the VMs) live inside a Host Pool; Application Groups (Desktop or RemoteApp) select what to publish from that pool; and a Workspace bundles Application Groups into the feed users see in the Windows App / Remote Desktop client.
concepts.whyItMatters: Users are assigned via RBAC (`Desktop Virtualization User`) to Application Groups—not directly to Host Pools or VMs—and an Application Group must be registered to a Workspace for users to see it.
gotchas: A single Host Pool can have multiple RemoteApp groups, but only ONE Desktop Application Group.
You cannot assign both a RemoteApp group and a Desktop group from the same host pool to the same user if you want clean separation—standard practice is dedicated pools or clear group boundaries.

checkQuestion.prompt: If a user has the Desktop Virtualization User role on an Application Group, why might the desktop icon still not appear in their Windows App feed?
choices: The Application Group is not associated with a Workspace
Start VM on Connect is disabled
The VM size is not D-series
checkQuestion.explanation: Users only see resources in their feed when the Application Group is linked to a Workspace (and the user has RBAC access to the Application Group).

concepts.title: Pooled vs. Personal Host Pools & Load Balancing
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: Pooled host pools share multi-session VMs (e.g., Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session) across many users; Personal host pools assign a dedicated 1:1 VM to each user (Automatic or Direct assignment). Pooled pools balance sessions using Breadth-first (spread evenly for best UX) or Depth-first (fill one host to `maxSessionLimit` before starting the next to save cost).
concepts.whyItMatters: Choosing Breadth-first vs. Depth-first and setting `maxSessionLimit` directly controls user density, noisy-neighbor risk, and autoscale efficiency.
gotchas: Breadth-first spreads load evenly across all running hosts, which prevents scaling plans from draining hosts unless the scaling plan overrides it during ramp-down.
Depth-first packs users onto fewer hosts, maximizing cost savings with autoscale, but risks CPU/memory contention if `maxSessionLimit` is set too high.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which load balancing algorithm fills one session host up to its maxSessionLimit before routing new connections to the next host?
checkQuestion.explanation: Depth-first saturates one host up to maxSessionLimit before moving to the next, making it ideal for cost-saving ramp-down scenarios.

concepts.title: The Five Control Planes of an AVD Estate
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: An AVD environment is never just Azure VMs—it spans five control planes: Azure (VMs, host pools, storage, Private Link), Entra ID (identities, groups, Conditional Access, Kerberos), Intune (OS policies, compliance, enrollment), Microsoft 365 (OneDrive KFM, Teams VDI, M365 Apps), and Power Platform (day-2 automation/approvals).
concepts.whyItMatters: In `avd-assess` and `avd-current-state`, every check and remediation hint is tagged with its `plane` so you know which team/repo owns the fix instead of blaming the wrong layer.
gotchas: Deploying AVD infrastructure in Azure without Entra Conditional Access or Intune baselines leaves endpoints and sessions unmanaged.
Teams VDI audio/video issues are often M365/protocol issues, not Azure VM sizing issues.

checkQuestion.prompt: In the avd-assess five-control-plane model, which plane owns Conditional Access policies and Microsoft Entra Kerberos?
checkQuestion.explanation: Entra ID owns identity, security groups, Conditional Access, and Entra Kerberos authentication.

concepts.title: Entra ID Join vs. Hybrid Join & Entra Kerberos
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Manage access and security
concepts.plainEnglish: Session hosts can be Microsoft Entra ID joined (cloud-native, no AD domain controllers needed) or Active Directory / Hybrid joined (traditional GPOs + AD DS). If hosts are Entra-joined and users are hybrid-synced, Microsoft Entra Kerberos lets them authenticate to Azure Files SMB shares without line-of-sight to a domain controller.
concepts.whyItMatters: Cloud-native Entra ID join removes the need to run domain controllers in Azure just for AVD, while Intune replaces traditional Group Policy Objects (GPOs).
gotchas: Entra-joined hosts require `targetisaadjoined:i:1` in RDP properties (or SSO enabled) for seamless sign-in.
Pure cloud-only Entra users (not synced from AD) cannot use AD-based NTFS ACLs with Entra Kerberos—check identity requirements carefully.

checkQuestion.prompt: What does Microsoft Entra Kerberos enable for Microsoft Entra ID-joined AVD session hosts?
choices: SMB authentication to Azure Files for hybrid-synced users without line-of-sight to AD domain controllers
checkQuestion.explanation: Entra Kerberos issues Kerberos tickets from Entra ID so hybrid users on Entra-joined hosts can access Azure Files SMB shares without contacting an AD domain controller.

concepts.title: Reverse Connect vs. RDP Shortpath (UDP)
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage networking for Azure Virtual Desktop
concepts.plainEnglish: By default, AVD uses Reverse Connect Transport: session hosts make an outbound TCP 443 connection to the AVD Gateway, so you never open inbound ports on your firewall. RDP Shortpath upgrades that session to direct UDP (via STUN/ICE for public networks or direct UDP 3390 for private/ExpressRoute/VPN networks) for much lower latency and better multimedia.
concepts.whyItMatters: UDP Shortpath dramatically improves interactive responsiveness, mouse/typing feel, and Teams media compared to TCP reverse connect.
gotchas: Client-side ZTNA/VPN agents that force-tunnel or block UDP silently break Shortpath and force fallback to TCP.
If Shortpath fails, sessions still connect via TCP Reverse Connect—so users complain of 'lag' rather than total outage.

checkQuestion.prompt: Why does AVD Reverse Connect not require opening inbound firewall ports to session hosts?
choices: The AVD agent on the session host initiates outbound TCP 443 connections to the AVD control plane
It requires a public IP on every VM
checkQuestion.explanation: Reverse Connect initiates outbound TLS (TCP 443) from the session host to the AVD service, avoiding any inbound internet exposure.

concepts.title: Conditional Access & Single Sign-On (SSO) for AVD
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Manage access and security
concepts.plainEnglish: Entra Conditional Access enforces MFA, compliant devices, or trusted locations at sign-in. Targeting the 'Azure Virtual Desktop' cloud app (and 'Windows Cloud Login' when Entra SSO is enabled) ensures users satisfy MFA once and pass through to the Windows session seamlessly.
concepts.whyItMatters: Without Entra SSO, users get prompted twice (once for the AVD client feed, once for Windows login). With SSO + Conditional Access, you get strong Zero Trust security with a single prompt.
gotchas: Excluding or misconfiguring 'Windows Cloud Login' in Conditional Access can cause unexpected MFA loops or blocked sign-ins.
Per-user legacy MFA breaks SSO; always use Conditional Access.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which Entra ID feature enforces MFA and device compliance checks before a user can access an AVD workspace?
checkQuestion.explanation: Conditional Access evaluates user, device, and location signals and enforces MFA or compliance before issuing tokens for Azure Virtual Desktop.

concepts.title: FSLogix Profile Containers & Redirections
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage user environments and apps
concepts.plainEnglish: On pooled multi-session hosts, users land on a different VM every day. FSLogix stores the user's entire Windows profile inside a VHD/VHDX container on a file share (like Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files) and dynamically attaches it at sign-in so the desktop feels persistent.
concepts.whyItMatters: Without FSLogix, users lose settings, Outlook caches, and Edge profiles on every sign-in—or bloat local OS disks.
gotchas: Always exclude Teams caches, temp folders, and OneDrive local cache where appropriate (`redirections.xml`) so VHDX containers don't bloat.
FSLogix Cloud Cache adds resilience across multiple storage providers, at the cost of extra local disk I/O and cache overhead.

checkQuestion.prompt: What problem do FSLogix Profile Containers solve in a pooled AVD host pool?
choices: They replace the Azure Load Balancer
They attach a user's profile VHDX from shared storage at sign-in so settings persist across non-persistent session hosts
They convert TCP traffic into UDP
checkQuestion.explanation: FSLogix mounts a remote VHD/VHDX container as the user's local profile at logon, giving persistent user state on pooled VMs.

concepts.title: App Attach / MSIX App Attach
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage user environments and apps
concepts.plainEnglish: Instead of baking every application into a monolithic golden image, App Attach (and MSIX App Attach) stores packaged apps in VHDX/CIM images on shared storage and dynamically mounts them onto session hosts at sign-in or host startup.
concepts.whyItMatters: Decoupling apps from the OS image dramatically reduces the number of golden images you must maintain and update.
gotchas: Not every legacy Win32 installer converts cleanly to MSIX—test app compatibility before committing to App Attach.
Session hosts need read access (and certificates if self-signed) to the App Attach storage share.

checkQuestion.prompt: What is the primary operational benefit of App Attach / MSIX App Attach in AVD?
choices: It eliminates the need for Azure Virtual Networks
It separates application delivery from the OS golden image by dynamically mounting app packages at runtime
checkQuestion.explanation: App Attach decouples apps from the base OS image, reducing golden image sprawl and simplifying app updates.

concepts.title: OneDrive Known Folder Move & Teams VDI Optimization
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage user environments and apps
concepts.plainEnglish: Redirecting Desktop, Documents, and Pictures to OneDrive (Known Folder Move + Files On-Demand) keeps user files out of the FSLogix VHDX, shrinking profile sizes. Meanwhile, Teams VDI WebRTC optimization offloads audio/video encoding from the Azure VM directly to the user's local endpoint.
concepts.whyItMatters: Without Teams media optimization, video calls route through the session host CPU and double-hop over RDP—crushing host density and call quality.
gotchas: Teams VDI optimization requires the Remote Desktop WebRTC Redirector Service installed on the session host AND a supported client.
Install M365 Apps on multi-session hosts with Shared Computer Licensing enabled.

checkQuestion.prompt: What happens if Teams VDI WebRTC media optimization is missing on a multi-session host pool?
choices: Audio/video processing falls back to the session host CPU and hairpins through the RDP channel, degrading call quality and host density
checkQuestion.explanation: Media optimization offloads WebRTC audio/video to the client endpoint; without it, the session host CPU encodes media and sends it over RDP.

concepts.title: Golden Images, Azure Compute Gallery & Validation Pools
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Create and configure session host images
concepts.plainEnglish: A golden image is your standardized Windows 11 Multi-session OS template (with M365, FSLogix agent, and OS optimizations), stored and replicated via Azure Compute Gallery. Before pushing a new image or AVD agent update to production, you test it in a Validation Host Pool.
concepts.whyItMatters: Setting `validationEnvironment: true` on a test host pool lets Microsoft roll out AVD service/agent updates there first, catching regressions before production users are hit.
gotchas: Never capture a golden image from a domain-joined VM without generalizing (`sysprep`)—and better yet, build images cleanly via pipeline/Packer or Azure VM Image Builder.
Remember to replicate Compute Gallery image versions to every Azure region where you deploy session hosts.

checkQuestion.prompt: What does setting Validation Environment = True on an AVD host pool do?
choices: It receives AVD agent and service updates earlier than non-validation pools so you can test before production rollout
checkQuestion.explanation: Validation host pools receive AVD service/agent updates first so admins can validate changes before they reach production pools.

concepts.title: Workload Placement: Pooled AVD vs. Personal AVD vs. W365
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: Not every user belongs on the same cloud desktop. Pooled AVD excels for shift/task workers sharing compute; Personal AVD fits users needing dedicated VMs, custom Azure VNet/GPU SKUs, or local admin; Windows 365 Enterprise fits knowledge workers who want predictable per-user monthly pricing managed entirely through Intune.
concepts.whyItMatters: In `avd-second-brain`, workload placement rules (`rules/workload-tiers.json`) match persona requirements (concurrency, GPU, local admin, cost predictability) to the right tier.
gotchas: Putting 24/7 dedicated users on Personal AVD without autoscale/hibernation can cost more than Windows 365 Enterprise.
Trying to force incompatible legacy single-user apps onto Windows 11 Multi-session causes stability issues.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which option best fits a shift-based call center of 300 workers using browser + M365 apps with overlapping 8-hour shifts?
choices: Pooled AVD (Windows 11 Multi-session) with an autoscale scaling plan
checkQuestion.explanation: Pooled AVD with multi-session hosts and a scaling plan maximizes concurrency and shuts down idle hosts between shifts.

concepts.title: Autoscale Scaling Plans, Start VM on Connect & FinOps
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: AVD Scaling Plans automate host power state across four phases: Ramp-up (boot hosts before shift), Peak (keep capacity ready), Ramp-down (drain and deallocate idle hosts), and Off-peak (minimum hosts, often 0). Pair with Start VM on Connect so off-peak users can still wake a host on demand.
concepts.whyItMatters: Compute is the largest cost in AVD. Deallocating idle hosts stops VM compute billing (you only pay for OS disks), and pairing budgets + action groups prevents surprise spend.
gotchas: Deallocating a VM stops compute charges, but managed OS disks and storage quotas still bill.
Always check that the scaling plan is assigned to the host pool AND the AVD service principal has the required RBAC role.

checkQuestion.prompt: If a scaling plan deallocates all session hosts during Off-peak hours, which feature allows an early-morning user to still connect?
checkQuestion.explanation: Start VM on Connect wakes a deallocated session host automatically when an authorized user initiates a session.

concepts.title: Contracts C11 (Current State) & C14 (Target State)
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: In the avd-ops family, repos never share live tenant secrets—they pass versioned, redacted JSON contracts. `C11` captures 'what is there now' (collected read-only by `avd-current-state`), and `C14` captures 'what we want to build' (read by `avd-landing-zone`).
concepts.whyItMatters: Redacted contracts let you reason about sizing, drift, and security posture across all five control planes without leaking tenant IDs, subscription IDs, or user names.
gotchas: Never put real tenant IDs, subscription IDs, IPs, or customer names into public repos or shared C11/C14 examples.
Dependencies point down: `avd-current-state` and `avd-landing-zone` work standalone without `avd-second-brain` or `avd-swarm`.

checkQuestion.prompt: In the AVD family contract model, what does Contract C11 represent?
choices: A raw Azure AD password dump
Redacted current-state facts collected read-only across the five control planes
A Terraform state file with secrets
checkQuestion.explanation: Contract C11 is the versioned, redacted snapshot of an environment's current state collected read-only by avd-current-state.

concepts.title: Benchmarking & C25 Empirical Evidence
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: Rather than guessing 'how many users fit on a D8s_v5' or 'how fast does FSLogix mount', `avd-benchmark` runs synthetic profiles (storage I/O, logon storm, multi-session density, autoscale, BCDR) and publishes redacted `C25` percentile distributions (p50/p95/p99) into `avd-assess`.
concepts.whyItMatters: Empirical percentiles turn guesswork ('it feels slow') into measurable baselines you can compare against your own Azure Monitor / AVD Insights telemetry.
gotchas: Averages hide logon storms—always look at p95 and p99 latency.
Synthetic benchmarks calibrate priors, but real-world LOB apps must still be validated with a pilot wave.

checkQuestion.prompt: Why do AVD benchmark profiles (C25) track p95/p99 percentiles instead of only averages?
choices: Averages cannot be computed in PowerShell
Averages hide tail latency spikes during burst events like morning logon storms
p99 is required by Entra Kerberos
checkQuestion.explanation: Logon storms and I/O contention affect tail latency (p95/p99) far more severely than the daily average.

concepts.title: Read First, Change With Approval & Never Leave the Meter Running
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Manage Azure identities and governance
concepts.plainEnglish: Safe cloud operations follow two rules: reading/assessing state is always free and safe, while any state-changing action requires an explicit human-approved plan; and any lab/sandbox deployment must tear down or stop billing when done without deleting the last copy of logs/evidence.
concepts.whyItMatters: This is the core operating model of `avd-second-brain` ('the brain thinks') and `avd-swarm` ('the swarm acts only on approved plans'), and it protects your own AZ-104/AZ-140 study labs from runaway Azure bills.
gotchas: Deleting a resource group removes VMs, but orphaned disks, public IPs, or Log Analytics retention can still incur charges if not audited.
Always keep redacted evidence/logs outside the deployment before tearing down a lab.

checkQuestion.prompt: In the Desktop DevOps model, what is the boundary between avd-second-brain and avd-swarm?
choices: avd-second-brain holds Owner credentials and deploys VMs directly
avd-second-brain never holds write credentials (it reasons/remembers), while avd-swarm only executes plans approved by a person
checkQuestion.explanation: The brain thinks (read-only memory and reasoning) and the swarm acts only through human-approved plans.

concepts.title: Azure Monitor, Log Analytics & AVD Insights
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Monitor and maintain Azure resources
concepts.plainEnglish: Azure Monitor collects platform metrics and activity logs, while a Log Analytics Workspace stores diagnostic logs and VM performance counters (via Azure Monitor Agent / Data Collection Rules). AVD Insights sits on top as a prebuilt workbook visualizing connection diagnostics, round-trip time (RTT), host capacity, and FSLogix/session health.
concepts.whyItMatters: Without Diagnostic Settings sending AVD host pool logs and VM perf counters to Log Analytics, you are flying blind during logon storms or protocol lag.
gotchas: Legacy Log Analytics agent (MMA) is retired—use Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) with Data Collection Rules (DCRs).
Long Log Analytics retention windows can quietly become a major recurring cost if left unbounded.

checkQuestion.prompt: What must be configured for AVD Insights to display session host performance counters and connection diagnostics?
choices: A Public IP on every session host
Diagnostic settings on AVD objects + Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) / Data Collection Rules sending data to a Log Analytics Workspace
checkQuestion.explanation: AVD Insights reads AVD service diagnostic logs and session host performance counters stored in a Log Analytics Workspace.

concepts.title: Azure Backup, Snapshots & BCDR for AVD
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Monitor and maintain Azure resources
concepts.plainEnglish: In AVD, you rarely back up pooled session host VMs because they are stateless and rebuilt from a golden image. Instead, you back up the stateful layers: FSLogix Azure Files shares (via Azure Backup / Recovery Services Vault snapshots), personal persistent VMs, and your IaC/golden image definitions.
concepts.whyItMatters: Backing up 50 stateless pooled VMs wastes money; losing the FSLogix file share without snapshots loses every user's profile.
gotchas: Deleting an Azure Files share or storage account without soft delete / vault retention destroys profiles immediately.
Cross-region BCDR requires either Cloud Cache / GRS-ZRS replication for profiles plus secondary-region host pool capacity.

checkQuestion.prompt: In a pooled AVD deployment, which component is the highest priority for regular Azure Backup snapshots?
choices: Stateless pooled session host OS disks
The Azure Files share storing FSLogix profile containers
checkQuestion.explanation: Pooled session hosts are stateless and redeployable from golden images; FSLogix profile containers hold stateful user data.

concepts.title: Azure Bastion & Secure Admin Access
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Configure and manage virtual networking
concepts.plainEnglish: Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH into VMs over TLS (port 443) through the Azure portal without assigning Public IPs to your VMs or opening port 3389/22 to the internet.
concepts.whyItMatters: Session hosts and jumpboxes in a secure AVD landing zone never have Public IPs; admins use Bastion (or private VPN/ExpressRoute) for break-glass troubleshooting.
gotchas: Azure Bastion requires a dedicated subnet named exactly `AzureBastionSubnet` (minimum `/26`).
Bastion bills hourly while deployed—tear it down or use Bastion Developer/on-demand in throwaway labs.

checkQuestion.prompt: What is the mandatory subnet name required when deploying Azure Bastion into a Virtual Network?
checkQuestion.explanation: Azure Bastion requires a dedicated subnet named exactly AzureBastionSubnet.

concepts.title: Hub-Spoke Egress, Azure Firewall & UDRs
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage networking for Azure Virtual Desktop
concepts.plainEnglish: In enterprise hub-spoke topologies, session hosts in a spoke VNet route internet-bound traffic through a hub Azure Firewall using a User-Defined Route (UDR: `0.0.0.0/0 -> Firewall Private IP`). The firewall must allow required AVD FQDN tags/service tags (`WindowsVirtualDesktop`, `AzureMonitor`, Entra, and Microsoft 365 endpoints).
concepts.whyItMatters: Blocking even one required AVD control-plane FQDN causes session hosts to show as Unavailable or fail agent registration.
gotchas: Do NOT perform TLS inspection on AVD control-plane/gateway FQDNs—certificate pinning breaks the agent.
Always check `avd-assess` endpoint map (`endpoints.yaml`) for required outbound FQDNs.

checkQuestion.prompt: What happens if an Azure Firewall performs TLS inspection on AVD control-plane traffic?
choices: Session hosts fail to register or connect because the AVD agent rejects untrusted/inspected certificates
checkQuestion.explanation: AVD control-plane traffic must bypass TLS inspection; replacing certificates breaks the AVD agent's trust.

concepts.title: RDP Properties & Device Redirection Hardening
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Manage access and security
concepts.plainEnglish: Host Pool RDP Properties control session behavior at connection time—such as whether users can redirect local drives (`drivestoredirect:s:`), clipboard (`redirectclipboard:i:`), printers (`redirectprinters:i:`), USB devices, or cameras, and whether Entra SSO (`enablerdsaadauth:i:1`) is enabled.
concepts.whyItMatters: Blocking local drive and clipboard redirection prevents data exfiltration from corporate AVD sessions to unmanaged personal endpoints.
gotchas: Disabling `redirectclipboard` hurts UX if users need copy/paste—balance security with persona needs, or restrict it only for unmanaged devices.
Microphone/camera redirection must remain enabled for Teams VDI calls.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which RDP property setting prevents users from mapping their local PC's C: drive into an AVD session?
checkQuestion.explanation: Setting drivestoredirect:s: (empty value) disables local drive redirection into the remote session.

concepts.title: FSLogix Cloud Cache & Multi-Region Resilience
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage user environments and apps
concepts.plainEnglish: FSLogix Cloud Cache (`CCDLocations`) writes profile changes to a local cache on the session host first and asynchronously replicates them to one or more remote SMB/Blob storage providers. If one file share goes down, users keep working from the local cache or secondary provider.
concepts.whyItMatters: Cloud Cache protects against transient SMB hiccups and enables active-active multi-region AVD profile resilience.
gotchas: Cloud Cache increases local session host OS/temp disk I/O and delays logoff slightly while flushing dirty blocks.
Do NOT configure both `VHDLocations` and `CCDLocations` simultaneously—Cloud Cache replaces `VHDLocations`.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which FSLogix registry setting enables Cloud Cache across multiple storage providers?
checkQuestion.explanation: CCDLocations configures FSLogix Cloud Cache providers; it replaces VHDLocations.

concepts.title: Intune Enrollment & Assignment Filters for AVD
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Create and configure session host images
concepts.plainEnglish: When Entra-joined AVD session hosts enroll in Microsoft Intune, Assignment Filters let you target policies specifically to `Windows 11 Multi-session` or specific host pool naming prefixes—without waiting for slow dynamic Entra groups to recalculate.
concepts.whyItMatters: Applying a single-user workstation BitLocker or sleep/hibernation policy to a multi-session AVD host can break sessions or lock out users.
gotchas: Multi-session Windows 11 supports device-targeted Intune policies well, while user-targeted policies have specific multi-session caveats.
Assignment filters evaluate at policy check-in time, making them much faster and safer than nested dynamic groups.

checkQuestion.prompt: Why are Intune Assignment Filters preferred over dynamic Entra groups for targeting AVD session host policies?
choices: Dynamic groups cannot contain Windows VMs
Assignment filters evaluate at device check-in without dynamic group membership recalculation lag, allowing fast, precise targeting by OS SKU or device name
checkQuestion.explanation: Assignment filters evaluate dynamically at check-in against device properties (like OS SKU or name), avoiding dynamic group sync delays.

concepts.title: Azure Policy Guardrails & Allowed Locations
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Manage Azure identities and governance
concepts.plainEnglish: Azure Policy evaluates resource properties at deployment time and continuously afterward—enforcing rules like 'Allowed locations', 'Require cost-center tag', or 'Deny public IPs on NICs'. Unlike RBAC (which controls WHO can act), Azure Policy controls WHAT configurations are allowed.
concepts.whyItMatters: In an AVD landing zone, Azure Policy guardrails (`enablePolicyGuardrails`) prevent someone with Contributor access from accidentally deploying a Public IP on a session host or spinning up GPUs in an unapproved region.
gotchas: RBAC + Policy work together: even an Owner cannot bypass a Deny policy without modifying the policy assignment.
Audit/Modify effects are safer to roll out first before switching to Deny.

checkQuestion.prompt: What is the difference between Azure RBAC and Azure Policy?
choices: RBAC controls who can perform actions on resources; Azure Policy enforces rules on the allowed properties and compliance state of resources
RBAC only works on storage accounts
checkQuestion.explanation: RBAC governs user/principal permissions (who), while Azure Policy governs resource configuration compliance (what).

concepts.title: Ephemeral OS Disks for Stateless Pooled Hosts
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: An ephemeral OS disk puts Windows on the VM's local temp disk or cache instead of a remote managed disk. Reads and writes are fast and reimaging is quick, but nothing on the OS disk survives: the VM can be restarted, reimaged or deleted, never stopped and deallocated.
concepts.whyItMatters: For a pooled, stateless host pool (profiles in FSLogix, apps from the image or App Attach) ephemeral disks cut OS disk cost and latency. avd-assess allows them only for pooled pools built from a session host configuration, on a size whose temp disk or cache fits the image, with autoscale creating and deleting hosts instead of deallocating them.
gotchas: No deallocation, snapshots, image capture, Azure Backup, Azure Site Recovery or Azure Disk Encryption on an ephemeral OS disk.
The image must fit: a 127 GiB marketplace image needs at least 127 GiB of temp disk or cache on the chosen VM size.
Dynamic autoscale with Minimum percentage of active hosts at 100% makes the plan create and delete hosts instead of starting and deallocating them.
The AVD prerequisites page and the dedicated ephemeral OS disk page disagree; avd-assess reads the dedicated page as the newer statement (see the row's note).

checkQuestion.prompt: Which operation is NOT supported on a session host that uses an ephemeral OS disk?
checkQuestion.explanation: Ephemeral OS disks live on local VM storage that is released on deallocation, so stop-deallocate isn't supported. Restart, reimage and delete are.

concepts.title: Managed Disk Encryption: SSE, Encryption at Host & Customer-Managed Keys
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
concepts.plainEnglish: Every managed disk is encrypted at rest by server-side encryption (SSE) with platform-managed keys, always on. Encryption at host extends that to the VM's temp disk and OS/data disk caches, encrypting data before it leaves the host. Customer-managed keys (CMK) live in Key Vault and attach through a disk encryption set when a requirement asks for key ownership.
concepts.whyItMatters: avd-assess's baseline is encryption at host for new session hosts (the landing zone's encryptionAtHost parameter) and no new Azure Disk Encryption, which retires on 2028-09-15. CMK is guidance only: use it when a compliance requirement calls for it, not by default.
gotchas: Encryption at host must be registered as a feature on the subscription before VMs can use it.
Azure Disk Encryption (BitLocker inside the guest) is a different feature from SSE and encryption at host; don't plan new deployments on it.
A disk encryption set needs access to the Key Vault key; losing the key or the access makes the disks unreadable.

checkQuestion.prompt: A security team wants session host temp disks and disk caches encrypted at rest without running BitLocker in the guest. What should you enable?
checkQuestion.explanation: Encryption at host encrypts temp disks and OS/data disk caches on the VM host. SSE alone covers the managed disks themselves, and Azure Disk Encryption runs inside the guest and is retiring.

concepts.title: Trusted Launch, Gen2 VMs & Confidential VMs
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: Trusted launch adds Secure Boot, a virtual TPM (vTPM) and boot integrity monitoring to Generation 2 VMs. It is the default for new AVD session hosts. Confidential VMs go further and encrypt VM memory against the host.
concepts.whyItMatters: The VM generation is fixed by the image: a Gen1 golden image can't produce Trusted launch hosts. avd-assess's baseline is Gen2 with Trusted launch, so the image pipeline has to build Gen2 images from the start.
gotchas: Trusted launch requires a Gen2 image; plan the Azure Compute Gallery image definition as Gen2 with the TrustedLaunch security type.
vTPM is what lets features like BitLocker key protection and device health attestation work on the host.

checkQuestion.prompt: Your golden image definition is Generation 1. What blocks you from deploying Trusted launch session hosts from it?
choices: Trusted launch requires a Generation 2 image
Trusted launch only works on personal host pools
Nothing; Trusted launch works with any image
checkQuestion.explanation: Trusted launch (Secure Boot and vTPM) is a Gen2-only capability, so the image must be Generation 2.

concepts.title: Screen Capture Protection & Watermarking
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement identity and security
concepts.plainEnglish: Screen capture protection is a session host policy (Intune settings catalog or Group Policy, from the AVD administrative template) that blocks remote content in screenshots and screen sharing on the client. Watermarking overlays QR codes carrying the Connection ID (or Device ID) so a photo of the screen can be traced back to the session in Log Analytics or AVD Insights.
concepts.whyItMatters: These are the AZ-140 answers for data exfiltration through the display. They are configured on the session host and enforced by the client, so they pair with redirection hardening (clipboard, drive and printer) rather than replacing it.
gotchas: Once watermarking is on, clients that don't support it fail to connect with a non-specific error; it doesn't apply to RemoteApp.
Neither feature is DRM: a phone camera still works, which is why the watermark exists.
avd-assess's security method leaves both items unknown until a host-side read exists, and cites watermarking as needing screen capture protection (ref:watermarking#needs-capture-protection).
The QR code's Connection ID is the CorrelationId in the WVDConnections table.

checkQuestion.prompt: A user photographs confidential data on an AVD desktop with a phone. Which feature lets admins trace the photo back to the session?
choices: Watermarking with a Connection ID QR code
checkQuestion.explanation: Watermarking embeds QR codes with the Connection ID; screen capture protection blocks OS-level capture but can't stop a camera.

concepts.title: Azure DNS Private Resolver for Hybrid Name Resolution
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Implement and manage virtual networking
concepts.plainEnglish: Azure DNS Private Resolver is a managed DNS service in a VNet. Its inbound endpoint gives on-premises DNS servers a private IP to conditionally forward Azure private zones (like privatelink.file.core.windows.net) to. Its outbound endpoint with a DNS forwarding ruleset lets Azure VNets resolve on-premises domains without running DNS VMs.
concepts.whyItMatters: avd-assess's network method requires every private endpoint name to resolve to its private address from the hosts, and a resolver where on-premises must resolve them. Without it, on-premises clients and admins reach Azure Files or AVD Private Link over public IPs or fail.
gotchas: Inbound endpoint = on-premises asks Azure; outbound endpoint + forwarding ruleset = Azure asks on-premises.
Each endpoint needs its own dedicated subnet delegated to the resolver.
The Private DNS zone still has to be linked to the VNet the resolver lives in.

checkQuestion.prompt: On-premises DNS servers must resolve an Azure Files private endpoint name to its private IP. What do you deploy in the hub?
choices: An Azure DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint, with an on-premises conditional forwarder for privatelink.file.core.windows.net
A public DNS zone for the storage account
An NSG rule allowing port 53 from the internet
A second storage account in the hub
checkQuestion.explanation: The inbound endpoint gives on-premises a private IP to forward the privatelink zone to; the resolver then answers from the linked Private DNS zone.

concepts.title: Scaling Plan Capacity Threshold, Minimum Hosts & Ramp-Down
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: Each scaling plan phase has a minimum percentage of hosts kept on and a capacity threshold. When used capacity (sessions divided by the available hosts' max session limit) crosses the threshold, autoscale starts another host. Ramp-down consolidates sessions onto fewer hosts and only frees a host when it has no sessions, unless you force sign-out after a notification.
concepts.whyItMatters: avd-assess publishes no number here (standing: gap): Microsoft says ramp up before users arrive and explains the threshold, so the method measures when sessions really arrive and how full the pool runs. The landing zone's own default is a 07:00 ramp-up with 20% of hosts and a 60% threshold.
gotchas: Disconnected sessions count as active, so a host with one disconnected user stays on; a 15 to 30 minute disconnected-session time limit lets a pool reach zero.
With single sign-on, locking the session disconnects it, which feeds the same problem.
A lower capacity threshold starts hosts sooner (more headroom, more cost); a higher one packs hosts tighter.
Each phase picks its own load-balancing algorithm: breadth-first spreads users at ramp-up, depth-first in off-peak keeps fewer hosts on.

checkQuestion.prompt: A pooled host pool has a max session limit of 10 and two hosts running with 13 sessions. With a 60% capacity threshold, what does autoscale do?
choices: Starts another host, because used capacity is 65%, above the 60% threshold
checkQuestion.explanation: Used capacity is 13 / (2 x 10) = 65%, which exceeds the 60% threshold, so autoscale turns on another host.

concepts.title: Personal Host Pools: Deallocation & Hibernation
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: Start VM on Connect only turns hosts on; it never turns them off. A personal host pool needs a personal scaling plan (or other automation) to deallocate or hibernate hosts after users disconnect or sign out. Hibernation saves memory to the OS disk so the user's desktop resumes where they left it.
concepts.whyItMatters: Personal desktops that never turn off are the classic AVD cost leak. avd-assess checks that personal pools have something that deallocates them (check asm-personal-deallocation).
gotchas: Hibernation isn't supported with FSLogix or App Attach, so it suits personal hosts with local profiles.
Hibernation must be enabled on each VM and needs a supported size and OS.
A personal scaling plan acts on disconnect and sign-out events with a wait time per phase.

checkQuestion.prompt: Personal session hosts with Start VM on Connect enabled are running 24x7. Why?
choices: Start VM on Connect deallocates hosts only on weekends
Start VM on Connect only starts hosts; a personal scaling plan or automation must deallocate or hibernate them
The capacity threshold is too low
checkQuestion.explanation: Start VM on Connect never deallocates. Pair it with a personal scaling plan that deallocates or hibernates hosts after disconnect or sign-out.

concepts.title: FSLogix Profile Container vs. Office (ODFC) Container
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Implement and manage user environments and apps
concepts.plainEnglish: The Profile Container holds the whole user profile. The Office Data File Container (ODFC) holds only Microsoft 365 cache data: Outlook OST, Teams, OneDrive cache, search. You can run one container with both, or split Office data into its own ODFC container.
concepts.whyItMatters: avd-assess's baseline is one container holding profile and Office data unless there's a stated reason to split; a split ODFC container isn't backed up or replicated (the data is recoverable from Microsoft 365). Splitting makes sense when Office caches need a different lifecycle or storage, or a separate profile solution owns the profile.
gotchas: ODFC is configured with its own registry keys (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\FSLogix\ODFC), separate from Profile Container settings.
With user data in OneDrive and SharePoint, the profile holds settings and caches; size and back up with that in mind.
Cloud Cache and backup plans that cover the profile container don't automatically cover a separate ODFC store.

checkQuestion.prompt: What does the FSLogix ODFC container store?
choices: The entire user profile, including desktop and documents
Only Microsoft 365 cached data such as the Outlook OST and Teams and OneDrive caches
checkQuestion.explanation: ODFC (Office Data File Container) redirects only Microsoft 365 cache data; the Profile Container holds the full profile.

concepts.title: AVD User Licensing, Per-User Access Pricing & Entra Licensing
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: AVD itself has no separate license for internal users: each user needs an eligible license (a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan, Windows Enterprise E3/E5, or an RDS CAL with Software Assurance for Windows Server hosts). External commercial users (customers, not employees or contractors) use per-user access pricing, billed through an Azure subscription. Conditional Access needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher, and Intune enrollment needs an Intune license.
concepts.whyItMatters: Licensing questions are easy AZ-140 points. avd-assess records that contractors count as internal users and that per-user access pricing belongs in its own subscription.
gotchas: Per-user access pricing is for external users only; it can't license your own employees or contractors.
Windows Server session hosts need RDS CALs; Windows 10/11 Enterprise multi-session hosts use the per-user Microsoft 365 or Windows entitlement.
Azure compute, storage and networking still bill separately from user licensing.

checkQuestion.prompt: A software vendor wants to deliver an app through AVD to its external customers, who have no Microsoft 365 licenses. What licenses the users?
choices: Per-user access pricing, billed through an Azure subscription
An RDS CAL for each customer without Software Assurance
No license is needed for external users
checkQuestion.explanation: Per-user access pricing exists for external commercial users and is billed monthly through a dedicated Azure subscription.

concepts.title: Azure Files Identity-Based Access: Share RBAC + NTFS ACLs
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Implement and manage storage
concepts.plainEnglish: Access to an Azure Files SMB share is checked twice: a share-level Azure RBAC role (Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor, Elevated Contributor or Reader) and then NTFS permissions on folders and files. The identity source is AD DS, Microsoft Entra Domain Services, or Microsoft Entra Kerberos; a storage account uses one at a time.
concepts.whyItMatters: Every FSLogix share depends on this. avd-assess's baseline is Entra Kerberos for Entra-joined hosts and AD DS with a rotated or non-expiring account password for domain-joined hosts, and it watches Kerberos ticket encryption since AES became the default.
gotchas: Users need Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor; admins setting NTFS ACLs need Elevated Contributor.
Using the storage account key bypasses identity-based access; keep it for break-glass only.
If the AD DS computer account password for the storage account expires, every sign-in that mounts a container fails.

checkQuestion.prompt: Users get access denied mounting their FSLogix container, though NTFS permissions on the share look correct. What else must be granted?
choices: A share-level role such as Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor
checkQuestion.explanation: Azure Files checks share-level RBAC first and NTFS ACLs second; both must allow access.

concepts.title: Availability Zones vs. Availability Sets for Session Hosts
concepts.domain: AZ-104: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
concepts.plainEnglish: Availability zones are physically separate datacenters within a region; spreading VMs across zones survives the loss of one. Availability sets spread VMs across fault and update domains inside one datacenter. A VM's zone or set is chosen when it's created and can't be changed later.
concepts.whyItMatters: avd-assess's baseline spreads session hosts across zones where the region has them (an availability set where it doesn't), with spare hosts for a lost zone. Zones are high availability, not disaster recovery: a regional outage still needs the DR model.
gotchas: You can't move an existing VM into a zone or set; redeploy it.
Profile storage should match: ZRS Azure Files keeps profiles available when a zone is lost.
Some VM sizes aren't offered in every zone; check before fixing the size.

checkQuestion.prompt: Which option protects a pooled host pool against the loss of a single datacenter in a region?
choices: Spreading session hosts across availability zones
checkQuestion.explanation: Availability zones are separate datacenters; an availability set only protects against rack and update failures within one datacenter.

concepts.title: Connection Errors: WVDErrors, ServiceError & Correlation IDs
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Monitor and maintain an Azure Virtual Desktop infrastructure
concepts.plainEnglish: AVD diagnostics land in Log Analytics as WVD tables: WVDConnections (each connection's states), WVDErrors (errors by code), WVDCheckpoints and WVDAgentHealthStatus. Each error carries a ServiceError flag: false means the cause is in your estate to fix, true means a service-side problem to raise with Microsoft using the CorrelationId.
concepts.whyItMatters: Triage starts by splitting admin-fixable errors from service errors. avd-assess reads errors as counts by code only, never user names or messages, and maps codes through the family's error-code map.
gotchas: Diagnostic settings must send the host pool and workspace logs to Log Analytics before any of this exists.
The CorrelationId ties a connection across WVDConnections, WVDErrors and WVDCheckpoints, and matches a watermark's Connection ID.
Session host health checks (WVDAgentHealthStatus) explain 'Unavailable' hosts: domain trust, FSLogix, stack listener, agent updates.

checkQuestion.prompt: A WVDErrors row shows ServiceError = false. What does that mean?
choices: Microsoft must fix it; open a support case
The error is caused by something in your deployment that an admin can fix
The user's client is out of date, always
checkQuestion.explanation: ServiceError false marks errors caused by the customer's configuration; true marks service-side errors to raise with Microsoft using the correlation ID.

concepts.title: Local Administrator Password Rotation (Windows LAPS)
concepts.domain: AZ-140: Plan and implement identity and security
concepts.plainEnglish: Every session host has a local administrator account. Windows LAPS gives each host a unique, rotated password stored in Microsoft Entra ID or AD DS, so one leaked image password can't unlock every host. Users never hold local admin rights on pooled hosts.
concepts.whyItMatters: avd-assess's guidance is to rotate the local administrator password with a solution like LAPS. The landing zone goes further and generates a random break-glass password on every build that is never stored.
gotchas: Windows LAPS is built into current Windows; configure it through Intune (account protection policy) or Group Policy.
Reading a LAPS password from Entra ID needs a specific role or permission and is audited.
A shared local admin password baked into the golden image is a lateral-movement risk across the whole pool.

checkQuestion.prompt: What does Windows LAPS provide for AVD session hosts?
choices: A unique, automatically rotated local administrator password per host, backed up to Entra ID or AD DS
checkQuestion.explanation: Windows LAPS manages and rotates a unique local admin password per device and stores it in Entra ID or AD DS.
